file_roles.evidence: Adds a BOOLEAN_COLUMNS list, an isBoolean(colName) helper and CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END generation, with the comment 'Special logic to turn booleans into integers. This is necessary because you cannot cast a boolean to an integer, according to the sql standard.' It exists only to keep generated ODBC metadata working once the cast is withdrawn.

comparable() allowed the comparison the report shows: the numeric branch returned 'compareWithTypeID.isNumericTypeId() || compareWithTypeID.isBooleanTypeId()' and the boolean branch likewise included isNumericTypeId(). Both boolean clauses are deleted, so 'where id = true' no longer type-checks.

convertible() drops '(otherType.isBooleanTypeId()) ||' from the numeric conversion list, and storable() changes from 'if ((otherType.isNumericTypeId()) || (otherType.isBooleanTypeId()))' to 'if (otherType.isNumericTypeId())'. This is the implicit boolean-to-number conversion the commit message says is being removed.

Removes 'otherType.isBooleanTypeId() ||' from the BIT/BLOB convertible list. The reported query compares a BIGINT with a boolean, not a BIT, so repairing this would not have prevented the reported failure; it removes the same non-standard conversion on another type.

convertible() previously returned true for everything except DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP and now returns '(otherType.isStringTypeId() || otherType.isBooleanTypeId())'. That blanket 'return true' is what permitted boolean to be converted to a numeric column in the reported predicate.

Both convertible() and storable() gain '|| otherType.isBooleanTypeId()'. This is permissive, not restrictive: boolean-to-string remains legal under the standard, so the target type compiler must now opt in once BooleanTypeCompiler stopped answering true for everything.

The LONGVARCHAR branch changes from 'return (otherType.isStringTypeId())' to '(otherType.isStringTypeId() || otherType.isBooleanTypeId())', with the comment updated to 'or CLOB or boolean'. The same forced opt-in as CLOBTypeCompiler.

rationale: The reported failure is a wrong result set, 'select id,date from inbox where id = true' returning one row where eleven were expected, with no exception and no log line, so neither a symptom file nor a log file can be placed. Three gold files hold the type rules that let the comparison compile at all and are causal; three more are the forced accommodations that keep standard-legal boolean-to-string conversions working, and one removes the same non-standard conversion on BIT, which was never on the reported path.
notes: java/build/org/apache/derbyBuild/ODBCMetadataGenerator.java is build-time tooling rather than product code, and TEST_PATH does not filter it, so it is in the gold set as a localisation target. Same class of benchmark defect as the Ambari perf script.
